The petitioner has filed petitions under Section 166 of M. V. Act for compensation of Rs. 10,00,000/- on account of accident taken place on or about 24.3.1995 at about 6.30 A.M. in the morning near Vada Village Borkampa, Dhansura when the claimant was going on his motorcycle no GUZ 1524 slowly on correct and left side of the road and as soon as he reached near the place of accident, the offending Mini Motor Truck No.GJ-V- 4638 came with full speed in rush and negligent manner dashed with claimant, wherein the claimant had received fracture and multiple injuries on different parts of the body.

It is further averred that due to injuries, the petitioner had taken prolong treatment for a pretty long time as indoor and outdoor patient in different hospitals for which he has spent huge amount being expenses.

It is further averred that at the time of accident, the petitioner was aged about 40 years old and was earning monthly income of Rs.15,000/- from service as Senior Clerk in Sbar Shit Centre, Dhansura as well as from the agriculture land.
Therefore, claimant has filed claim petition seeking compensation with cost and interest against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1 and 2 - driver and owner have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Insurance Company has appeared and has filed its written statement / objections by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.

The oral as well as

After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

sentences.text:
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the Insurance Company and Cross Objection is filed by the claimant for enhancement.
3. Learned advocate Mr. Palak Thakkar for the Insurance Company has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has submitted that amount of award is on higher side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like prospective income of the deceased, negligence, liability and family circumstances, etc.
It is submitted that learned Tribunal failed to consider that there was no documentary proof in support of claimant's oral say that his actual income was Rs.10,000/- to Rs.12,000/- per month.

It is submitted that learned Tribunal failed to consider disability certificate issued by Dr. Hiren Maniar,
wherein claimant's permanent physical impairment was assessed at 10% body as whole.
It is also submitted that learned Tribunal has erred in applying multiplier of 15.
He has submitted that the appeal may be allowed.

4. Per contra, Mr. Maulik Shelat, learned advocate for claimant has submitted that learned Tribunal has erred in not NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2348/2009 ORDER DATED: 01/10/2024 undefined considering prospective income of the injured claimant without any reasons assigned in impugned judgment.
It is submitted that due to disablement, the claimant is not in position to do his job freely as he was doing prior to accident.
It is also submitted that claimant has produced all evidence to prove his agricultural income.
It is submitted that learned Tribunal has erred in awarding less compensation under head of actual loss of income.

It is submitted that learned Tribunal ought to have considered that claimant has sustained serious injuries and taken best rest, so learned Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering.

It is therefore,
submitted to allow the Cross Objection and enhance the awarded compensation.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2348/2009 ORDER DATED: 01/10/2024 undefined award passed by the Tribunal.
From the record, it transpires that the injured was aged about 40 years and was working as Senior Clerk in Sbar Shit Centre, Dhansura.
It appears that two vehicles are involved in the accident and petitioner was plying motorcycle at the time of accident and he sustained injuries.

The claimant has produced documentary evidence viz. complaint, panchnama of place of accident,
driving license of opponent no.1, proof of ownership and insurance of offending ehicle, injury certificate, medical bills etc.
The driver and owner of the offending vehicle have not stepped into witness box.

Learned Tribunal has discussed the issue vividly in para 11 to 17, which reads as under :-
"11.

In the circumstances, it is for the tribunal to see as to whether the petitioner has succeeded in proving the accident and the vehicle involved in the accident and this tribunal is of considered view that strict rules of evidence, such as proof beyond reasonable doubt in criminal cases and preponderance of probabilities in civil cases would not apply in the claim proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act.
12. The above view is supported by the judgment reported in 2006(2) CACC 454 wherein it is held that "7.

It has to be kept in mind that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation, the very object of which is to grant relief to the legal heirs of persons unfortunate enough to have died or sustained injuries, in a motor accident."

It is further held that:
"As such, strict rules of evidence such as proof beyond reasonable doubt in criminal cases and preponderance of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2348/2009 ORDER DATED: 01/10/2024 undefined probabilities in civil cases, cannot be made applicable to claims under this Act, Otherwise, the very purpose of its enactment would be nullified.
It is sufficient that there should be evidence on record on scrutiny of which the M.A.C. Tribunal arrives at a conclusion and gives a finding."

13. This tribunal also believes and is aware that of course the Motor Vehicles Act is beneficiary law to victims who have suffered a loss in vehicular accident but at the same time it cannot help to dependents/injured who are in fact having all means to earn and to live luxurious life by fruits to be earned from death/injury caused in accident.

14. Thus, in view of over all evidence on record and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, the question as to what is just compensation to be awarded by this tribunal being compensation in the petition has remained to be decided by the tribunal.
15. In this regard, it may be stated that Section 168 of Motor 15. Vehicles Act empowers the Claims Tribunal to "make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just.
Therefore, the only requirement for determining the compensation is that it must be "just".
There is no other limitation or restriction on its power for awarding just compensation.
The function of the Tribunal is to award "just" compensation which is reasonable on the basis of evidence produced on record.

16. Moreover, this tribunal further believes that in an 16. appropriate case where from the evidence brought on record if the Tribunal considers that the claimants are entitled to get more compensation than claimed, the Tribunal may also pass such award.

The only embargo is-it should be "JUST"
compensation that is to say, it should be neither arbitrary nor fanciful nor unjustifiable from the evidence.

sentences.text: This tribunal is also of the opinion that the compensation to a victim of a motor vehicle accident or in case of a fatal accident to the legal representatives is awarded under two heads, viz. special damages - which are suffered by the victim or the legal representatives and general damages - which include compensation for pain and sufferings, loss of amenities, earning capacity and prospective expenses including expenses for medical treatment.

These views of the tribunal are supported by the case of Nagappa Vs. Gurudayal Singh and Ors. of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in 2003(1)
G.LR. (S.C.) p.897: 2003(2) SCC P. 274.
17.

entities.text:

sentences.text:
Thus, having regard to over all evidence and bearing in mind the principle of "Just Compensation", this tribunal is of the view that so far as the quantum is concerned, the petitioner has replied in his cross examination that he has been drawing salary of about Rs. 10,000/- to Rs.
12,000/- per month as on the date of deposition and his service is not terminated.
Thus, from this evidence, it is evident that the opponents have not successfully disproved the income of the petitioner.
The petitioner has miserably failed to prove income from agriculture land.

However, this court believes that considering petitioner's income is of about Rs. 10,000/- to Rs.12,000/- p.m. as on the date of deposition, if his monthly income at the time of accident is assessed one and half less ie. Rs.7.500/- or thereabout, it would not be exaggerated and thus, bearing in mind, if the prospective income of petitioner is accepted as Rs. 10,000/-, it would be reasonable, proper and just as per view of this tribunal for want of any contrary evidence in rebuttal.

The petitioner has also proved disability at 25% as per certificate vide Exh.53 proved by the oral evidence of evidence of Doctor vide Exh.52 and considering his permanent disability arrived at out of injuries caused, if the petitioner is awarded Rs.15,000/- being pain, shock, suffering, it would be justified.

The petitioner's age of 40 years is not disproved and not challenged successfully during cross examination and therefore, considering his age, if 15 multilpliers are adopted, it would be legal and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2348/2009 ORDER DATED: 01/10/2024 undefined would meet ends of justice."
8.
For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal and Cross Objection are dismissed.
The impugned judgment and award is confirmed.

8.2 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8.3 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.4 Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
